record.paper_title: Several Open Problems in Operator Theory
record.original_question: Which Frechet spaces admit a chaotic operator? An operator T on a Frechet space is chaotic when it is hypercyclic, meaning some vector has dense orbit {T^n x : n in N}, and when its periodic points are dense, where a periodic point is a vector x for which T^n x = x for some integer n at least 1.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a separable infinite-dimensional Fréchet space (i.e., a complete metrizable locally convex topological vector space) over $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. A continuous linear operator $T:X\to X$ is said to be:

(i) hypercyclic if there exists a vector $x\in X$ whose orbit $\{T^n x : n\in\mathbb{N}\}$ is dense in $X$;

(ii) chaotic (in the sense of Devaney) if it is hypercyclic and its set of periodic points $\mathrm{Per}(T) := \{x\in X : T^n x = x \text{ for some integer } n\geq 1\}$ is dense in $X$.

Characterize, in terms of intrinsic topological/linear structural properties, those separable infinite-dimensional Fréchet spaces $X$ on which there exists at least one chaotic continuous linear operator $T:X\to X$.
artifact.status_search_result: The general characterization remains open. Positive results are known: every separable infinite-dimensional Banach (and many Fréchet) spaces support hypercyclic operators (Ansari, Bernal-González, Bonet–Peris), and spaces with an unconditional Schauder decomposition support chaotic (and frequently hypercyclic) operators (Bonet–Martínez-Giménez–Peris, De la Rosa–Frerick–Grivaux–Peris). On the negative side, Bonet–Martínez-Giménez–Peris (2001) exhibited a separable Banach space admitting no chaotic operator. No intrinsic characterization of Fréchet spaces admitting a chaotic operator is known.

status_evidence.title: A Banach space which admits no chaotic operator
status_evidence.snippet: Bonet, Martínez-Giménez, Peris construct a separable Banach space admitting no chaotic operator.
status_evidence.claim: Negative examples exist; characterization of which spaces admit chaotic operators is not resolved.

status_evidence.title: Frequent hypercyclicity, chaos, and unconditional Schauder decompositions
status_evidence.snippet: Banach spaces with an unconditional Schauder decomposition support chaotic and frequently hypercyclic operators.
status_evidence.claim: Partial positive results provide sufficient structural conditions for existence of chaotic operators.

status_evidence.title: Linear Dynamical Systems (survey) — Gilmore
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of linear dynamics listing open problems including chaos on Fréchet spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Characterization of Fréchet spaces admitting chaotic operators is mentioned as an open direction.
